Australia's Hyundai Sonata Gets Discontinued, New i30 Sedan Hybrid Taking Over in 2027
49 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Can you believe Hyundai Australia dealers couldn't sell more than 8 examples of the Sonata in October 2026? That figure says more than enough about the South Korean model's predicament, especially when you find out that Toyota Australia dealers moved 930 units of the hybrid-only Camry during the same month.
Speaking of which, the Sonata's problem gets a lot more serious when you search for the year-to-date registration data. Precisely 187 units were moved through October 2026, resulting in a very disappointing monthly average. Hyundai Australia has now confirmed that Sonata production for Down Under came to a screeching halt in October 2026, ending a run that began in 1989.
More than 73,000 units were sold thus far, and between you and me, that's a pitiful tally for a model competing in such a mainstream segment. According to WhichCar?, which cites Hyundai Australia’s Guido Schenken, the midsizer won't get a direct successor in this part of the world. The CN8-generation i30 Sedan Hybrid will take its place, a.k.a. the redesigned Elantra Hybrid.
Revealed in June at the Busan Motor Show, the CN8 is called Avante back home and is larger in every respect compared to the preceding Elantra. According to Hyundai Motor America's tech specs, the new compact is leaning into the mid-size segment, being 3.4 inches longer and 1.2 inches wider. These dimensions make it a pretty good indirect successor to the Sonata N Line in Australia.
It's also taller, but curiously enough, its drag coefficient is better. The drag coefficient figure is all the more interesting once you take in the low-poly design language, which includes flared fenders by default. Returning to a classic three-box profile with a flat roofline, the 2027 model can be described as both sharp and industrial. The interior, meanwhile, is on the minimalist side.
Photo: Hyundai Back in Australia, the current-gen Sonata rolled out in 2021. A facelift arrived in the latter part of 2023, bringing a full-width front lighting signature, a far more angular front bumper, a revised dashboard, and extra tech. From a mechanical standpoint, it's a solid car that offers plenty of muscle as well, courtesy of a 2.5-liter turbo inline-four mill that is joined by a wet-clutch DCT.
The N Line is most definitely a looker, but as with every N Line specification, it's mostly show rather than extra driving excitement. While it may look considerably more ambitious than the Toyota Camry, the people have voted with their wallets in favor of the far more boring and way more frugal alternative.
Hyundai Australia's best year for the Sonata was 1997, when 7,390 units found buyers. For a brief period, it wasn't even called Sonata. The i45 nonsense stopped in early 2013, and the Sonata nameplate returned for 2015 with the seventh generation. The year-to-date sales recorded through October 2026 put the Sonata behind some of the brand's electric vehicles, including the Ioniq 6.
The Camry recorded 10,401 deliveries in the first ten months of the current year, up 22.2 percent from the same period last year. Adding insult to injury, the Sonata N Line costs more than the top-of-the-range Camry SL grade as of this writing.
Via // WhichCar?
